**In the diagram:** row 5, *Effort* (`assign_effort`). Its measures, richest first: pressure (with gear size) → static
gear (soak, hauls) → kW-hours (with engine power) → hours (pings only) → fishing days (days at sea). Fishing pings
only.

## The problem

- Effort is what the groups map most. 269 of the reading map's topic rows fall on this row, in all 13 reports.
- Each measure needs something more than the last. Hours need only pings, kW-hours need the engine, swept area
  needs the gear's width, and static-gear effort needs the gear itself.

## What the groups say

- Surface area trawled per cell (WGSFD 2013, p. 5); swept area with standard gear values (WGSFD 2014, p. 37); swept
  area from gear width (WKSSFGEO 2022, p. 9).
- Making effort comparable across years (WGSFD 2014, p. 8); AIS gaps inflate fishing hours (WGSFD 2019, p. 11).
- Days at sea, effort and capacity (WKSSFGEO 2022, pp. 12, 15); fishing days across three sources (WKSSFGEO2 2023,
  pp. 56-57).
- Effort for passive gears: track length against time at sea, and soak time (WKSSFGEO2 2023, p. 5); vessel effort
  against gear effort (WKSSFGEO2 2023, p. 26).

## From ramb's articles

- No article on effort yet. The *flow* article names `rb_cap_effort()`, and *gear* gives the widths that pressure
  needs.

## The measures, richest first

### Pressure, with gear size

- Case: swept area of the survey tows, from BENTHIS widths. Data: `trawlsurveytows`, `trawlsurvey`,
  `benthis_parameters`.
  - Graphic: the swept area of each tow as a ribbon on the map; swept area against tow length.

### Static gear: soak and hauls

- Case: soak time per set, and hauls counted per trip. Data: `wkssfgeo2_it_pots`, `wkssfgeo2_irl_pots`.
  - Graphic: soak time distribution; hauls per trip against hours at sea.

### kW-hours

- Case: hours times engine power. Data: `dansk` with a simulated register of power.
  - Graphic: kW-hours by vessel.

### Hours

- Case: the interval to the next ping, with long gaps capped. Data: `dansk`.
  - Graphic: hours per ping, uncapped against capped; the share of effort in long gaps.

### Fishing days

- Case: calendar days with fishing, per vessel. Data: every ramb set with fishing labels.
  - Graphic: fishing days against hours fished, one dot per vessel-month.

## Methods compared

- Hours by ping interval against hours by track length per cell. Graphic: the two maps side by side.
- The three fishing-day definitions (logbook date, sales note, track). Graphic: one bar per definition for the same
  vessels.

## What if a source is missing

- No engine power: hours only. No gear width: no pressure. No gear: no static-gear effort. Show a table of which
  measures survive.
- Sparse pings: hours inflated across gaps. Show by thinning `dansk`.

## Checking it

- Effort from the track against effort from the logbook for the same trips.

## In the ICES data call

- The data call takes the interval within the trip, kW-hours, and swept area (sfdSAR), in 0.05° c-squares.

## With ramb

- `rb_add_effort()`, `rb_cap_effort()`, `rb_calc_step_time()`, `rb_predict_gear_width()`, `rb_fill_gear_width()`.

## Not yet in ramb

- Static-gear pressure (net length × soak time); hours apportioned by track length per cell; fishing days as a
  function.
